title: Inside the Harness
description: A model on its own can only predict text. This visual companion to the written course shows how a harness turns that text into work, and what every request really costs.

sections.title: Harness anatomy
sections.summary: The six parts that surround the model, and why the model cannot act without them.

sections.title: The agent loop
sections.summary: Watch the harness re-send the whole conversation on every request.

sections.title: The context window
sections.summary: Fixed overhead, piling-up tool results, and what compaction throws away.

sections.title: Token growth
sections.summary: Why total input grows much faster than the context you end with.

sections.title: Choosing an extension
sections.summary: Instructions files, skills, subagents, hooks, MCP servers, and plugins, compared.

sections.title: Inside an extension
sections.summary: What an MCP server, a skill, a subagent, and a plugin each add to every request, and when.

sections.title: Flow simulations
sections.summary: Trace permission decisions, verification evidence, and where request data travels.
sections.activity: Change a setup. Follow the consequences.

sections.title: Final review
sections.summary: Mixed questions from every section, plus choosing and using a harness safely.

curriculum.title: Build a harness
curriculum.concept: Follow the loop from a model request to a tool result.
curriculum.prompt: Before you step forward, predict which earlier messages the next request must include.
curriculum.lab: Complete the loop exercise, then compare its request bodies with the solution.

curriculum.title: Configure hard controls
curriculum.concept: Separate model instructions from controls that execute outside the model.
curriculum.prompt: Choose a tool request. Toggle hooks, deny, ask, and allow rules, then predict which gate stops the call.
curriculum.lab: Compare the naive and strict policies, then test your own deny rules and hooks.

curriculum.title: Engineer the context
curriculum.concept: See how fixed overhead and growing results compete for a finite window.
curriculum.prompt: Increase tool-result size in the simulator. Predict when compaction will happen, then check what survives.
curriculum.lab: Compare instructions-file sizes in Lab A and trace information loss in Lab B.

curriculum.title: Verify the work
curriculum.concept: Turn an agent’s completion claim into evidence you can review.
curriculum.prompt: Compare a source fix with a weakened test. Inspect the diff and remove the source fix to challenge the test.
curriculum.lab: Run Claim versus evidence, inspect the test diff, then remove the fix to prove the test catches the bug.

curriculum.title: Extend the harness
curriculum.concept: Inspect when an extension loads, what runs, and which context pays for it.
curriculum.prompt: Switch between MCP, skill, subagent, and plugin lenses. Disable a component in the ledger and explain the change.
curriculum.lab: Run the MCP probe and skill triage script, then compare their outputs with the visual.

curriculum.title: Operate on an air gap
curriculum.concept: Account for processes, destinations, and retained data beyond the model.
curriculum.prompt: Block public egress, then trace which internal and local copies still retain file content.
curriculum.lab: Use the module’s egress audit and model-capability checks. Trace endpoint, gateway, and transcript storage.

curriculum.title: Observe token usage
curriculum.concept: Distinguish final context, total input, fresh tokens, and cached input.
curriculum.prompt: Compare focused and broad sessions, toggle caching, and explain why cached input still counts toward total input.
curriculum.lab: Read a usage report, find the cache miss, then measure a session with less overhead.
